content.thinking:
I need to write the whole file carefully in one pass without testing. I'm deciding on a pose for the phoenix—standing on talons with wings spread upward-outward so it touches the floor, roughly 1.3 meters tall.

Mapping out construction details: a swept body with tapering radius from tail to chest, a curved neck sweeping up to the head, a sphere head with a gold beak spike and flame-shaped crest feathers, eye decals, and legs built from thigh-to-knee-to-foot rods ending in clawed toes near the floor.

For the wings, I'm sketching arm bones sweeping from shoulder to elbow to wrist, with fanned flight feathers extruded as pointed leaf shapes oriented along the wing plane.

Writing feather outline function...

Now I'm thinking through the color gradients, binning feathers by length into gold/orange/red tones, and planning how the primary feathers fan outward from the wrist with varying directions, from outward-up at the top to backward-down toward the tip.

Laying out primaries, secondaries, and covert layers along the wing's leading edge, with lengths tapering and slight offsets for layering depth.

For orienting each feather, I need to handle the degenerate case where direction is nearly aligned with the z-axis — I'm defining a local frame using a horizontal-ish up vector crossed with the feather direction to get a stable thickness axis.

Now I'm moving on to the arm bones with sweep paths and orange paint, then planning the tail with seven flowing plumes.

Writing tail plume geometry...

I'm applying a fur-edge paint to the body using orange and gold tones along the z-axis, then scattering small feather-shaped cards across the surface for chest detail.

Since painted surfaces can't glow, I'm planning separate extruded flame shapes—rising from the head crest, wing tips, and tail—as flat-colored teardrop curls with sharp points, oriented to flow outward and given a glow effect.

Fixing the orthogonal basis with a reference vector approach, then placing small flame licks at the primary feather tips with the base pulled slightly inward from the tip. I'm also considering adding floating embers and golden ornamental details—a gemmed collar, forehead gem, leg anklets, and tail ribbons for a Genshin-style look.

I'm orienting torus rings along the neck tangent and shin direction for the collar and anklets, and setting up an eye decal on the head sphere with careful size scaling relative to head radius, guarding against a null hit result.

Now I'm positioning the beak as a tapered spike extending forward and down from the head center, with a shorter lower beak, then planning cheek plumes and a crest built from small flame-shaped extrusions in gold.

For the wing, I'm sketching shoulder, elbow, and wrist anchor points, then sweeping an armature curve through them with varying radii to form the main wing structure, adding covert feather rows along the shoulder for layered detail.

Still working out feather placement...

Still working out feather placement and overlap...

For a flame gradient I'll go crimson at the base, orange in the middle, and bright yellow at the tips, with cel shading handling shadow hue-shifts automatically on the lit paint. I'll cache textures by rounding length to limit variety, keeping the texture count manageable.

For the tail ribbon, I'm figuring out the radius taper function and cross-section shape so the ribbon tapers to a point at the tip, accepting some uncertainty in the normal orientation along the backward-curving path.

Now I'm designing the talon spikes: three forward toes and one back toe per foot, each a tapering cone angled downward to a sharp tip, sized so the base sits flush at the foot while the point reaches near the ground. I'm also planning the gold scale coloring for the legs.

Still shaping leg geometry...

Now I'm working out the body and neck proportions, defining the torso path from tail base to chest and curving the neck upward toward the head position.

I'm also checking overall scale—total height, wingspan, and feather lengths—adjusting them so the phoenix's wings look proportionate when raised, with feathers fanning backward and down from the wrist.

I'm adding a chest gem for the phoenix, raycasting from the front at chest height to find the body surface and stick a glowing gold-set gem there, accepting the risk of a null hit at that position.

Now I'm planning the head crest: five flames fanning from the back of the head in yellow-orange gradients, glowing via the glow helper, plus small accent gems. I'm also designing flame tips for the wing feathers, positioning them at each primary and secondary tip with a slight upward direction and glow applied.

I'm adding gold filigree details—trim bands on the arms, gold ring ornaments at elbows and wrists with hanging tasseled cards, anklets with similar tassels, and a decorative gold ring at the tail base. For the eyes I'm using an anime-style iris texture, and I'm starting to write SVG textures for the feather cards with gradient fills transitioning from red to gold.

Writing gradient and path code...

For scattering cards onto the body surface, I'm figuring out how the surface scatter function works with the sweep geometry, checking whether it accepts a body tube target directly based on the docs example.

I'm also thinking through scattering cards onto the neck separately since the surface target may not support an array of parts, setting the flow direction and size variance for the cards, and deciding to add a few floating ember particles around the figure rather than a full floor ring of flames, since those would hang unnaturally at ground level.

Writing extrusion parameters for feather shapes...

Defining extrude parameters now, then setting up a cel-shaded color palette with warm reds, oranges, golds, and creams for the feather. I'm writing a paint function that blends colors along the feather's length based on a normalized position value, caching the result per length.

Still writing color gradient logic...

Now I'm planning the shoulder sphere, covert feather rows with layered offsets, and starting the actual feather-generation function that builds vectors from position and direction inputs.

Writing feather outline geometry...

Now I'm setting up the wing loop, building each arm as a catmull-rom path through shoulder, elbow, and wrist points, then laying down rows of secondary feathers along that curve.

Still defining feather layer parameters...

Still shaping the tail plumes...

Still defining feather paints...

For the forehead gem I'm attaching a small red sphere into a gold setting on the head surface, then adding a neck collar by placing a flattened gold torus at a point along the neck sweep curve, orienting it with the tangent direction and matching the local radius there.

Now I'm working out rings for the arms, placing toruses at tangent points along the arm path near the elbow and wrist with different radii and tube thickness, and planning a tassel hanging from the wrist ring using a frame positioned below the ring and oriented downward.

For the legs, I'm adding anklet toruses at a point along the leg path, then designing talons: three front toes splayed at angles with flat colored bases, dark sharp claw tips, and a rear toe pointing backward-down.

I'm scattering small glowing octahedra embers near the wrist using a seeded RNG, considering feather card textures for the body and chest bib with a gold tint, then wiring up the builder export that assembles everything into the final phoenix object.

Now I'm writing a flame-shaping helper that extrudes a tapered flame silhouette oriented along a given direction vector, using cross products to build a local coordinate frame for the extrusion.

Confirming no edge crossings in the outline, then checking the smoothing radius against the short closing edge near the tip to make sure the corner cuts don't overlap on such a narrow shape.

Now I'm writing the arm and neck sweeps with their catmull paths, radius tapers, and colors, then moving on to the wing row generation code.

Adding flame tips to primaries...
